Guys, one small feedback from a viewer who genuinely enjoys the show and has even attended a live Lavari episode. First of all, thank you for all the fun and entertainment, you guys are naturally hilarious and the chemistry between all of you is amazing.

But honestly, I would really like if guests were allowed to speak more during the episodes. Even in this episode, there were a lot of interruptions, and if you look at the comment section, many viewers seem to feel the same way. I understand the original live recordings are much longer, but while editing, it would be great if more meaningful conversations from the guests could be included.

For example, in the Devaki episode, it felt like she hardly got enough time to properly share her thoughts. On the other hand, Dharmesh sir’s episode was one of the best because he was given enough space to speak, and that made the episode feel more engaging and memorable.

You guys do not need to constantly prove how funny or entertaining you are, everyone already knows that and loves you for it. Your punches and reactions are great, but the guest should ideally have the highest talking time in their own episode.

No offense at all, just genuine feedback from someone who truly enjoys watching Lavari and wants the conversations to feel even better. Keep doing amazing work.

In karnataka and also Tamil Nadu- we call it bagala Bhaath- we cook the rice a bit soft and well done- donuts soft and mushy hot and we sometimes even add a little milk hot first in hot rice to make it mashed well mushy n creamy soft so it tastes extra creamy soft- then we add thick sour curds to the mashed soft rice add salt and mix well then add grated thin carrots , some fine chopped or grated skinned and seeded cucumbers too if we have fresh ones at home- yes and you can add pomegranate seeds for a seeet tangy taste some people add green grapes too for sweet sour taste - then put tadka of mustard seeds chana dal urad dal curry leaves , dhania leaves , 1/4 th piece ginger , chopped or slit green chillies without seeds n directed chillies too if you like it spicy - add this tadka and mix well with curd rice n enjoy Bagala Bhaath! *"Restaurant-style Veg Burrito Bowl Recipe"* *_Ingredients:-_* *For the Paneer:* * Paneer: 200g (cut into large cubes) * Butter: 1 tsp * Chilli Flakes: 1 tsp * Oregano/Mixed Herbs: 1 tsp * Salt: To taste *For the Rajma (Beans):* * Boiled Rajma (Kidney Beans): 1/2 cup * Garlic: 1 tsp (finely chopped) * Onion: 4 tbsp (finely chopped) * Tomato: 4 tbsp (finely chopped) * Schezwan Chutney: 1 tsp * Cooking Oil: 1 tbsp * Salt: To taste * Water: As needed *For the Cilantro Lime Rice:* * Cooked Rice: 1 cup (preferably sticky variety like Indrayani or Govind Bhog) * Butter: 1 tbsp * Coriander Leaves: A handful (finely chopped) * Lemon Juice: From half a lemon * Salt: To taste *For the Sautéed Salad:* * Onion: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Yellow Capsicum: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Red Capsicum: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Boiled Corn: 2 tbsp * Mixed Herbs: 1/2 tsp * Chilli Flakes: 1/2 tsp * Cooking Oil: 1 tsp * Salt: To taste *For the Yogurt Dressing:* * Greek Yogurt: 1/2 cup (or thick hung curd) * Garlic: 4 cloves (grated) * Black Pepper: 1/5 tsp * Coriander/Mint Leaves: Finely chopped * Salt: To taste *Additional Toppings:* * Avocado: 1 (sliced or mashed into guacamole) * Cherry Tomatoes: Handful (halved) * Lemon Juice & Salt: For seasoning the tomatoes * Tortilla Chips/Nachos: For crunch *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Paneer* Heat 1 tsp butter in a pan. Add 200g paneer cubes. Season with 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp oregano, and salt. Sauté on medium flame for about a minute until lightly golden. Avoid overcooking to keep the paneer soft. Remove and set aside. *2. Cook the Rajma* In the same pan, heat 1 tbsp oil. Add 1 tsp chopped garlic, 4 tbsp onions, and 4 tbsp tomatoes. Sauté until soft. Add 1/2 cup boiled rajma, salt, and 1 tsp Schezwan chutney for a zingy flavor. Add a little water and cook on low flame for 5 minutes. Mash a few beans with a masher for a thick texture, then dry out the excess moisture. Set aside. *3. Make Cilantro Lime Rice* Heat 1 tbsp butter in a pan. Add 1 cup cooked rice, salt, and plenty of fresh coriander leaves. Toss for 10 seconds to infuse the flavor. Turn off the heat and squeeze in lemon juice. Mix well and set aside. *4. Sauté the Salad* Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan. Add sliced onions, red and yellow capsicums, and boiled corn. Season with 1/2 tsp mixed herbs, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes, and salt. Sauté quickly just to remove the rawness while keeping the crunch. Set aside. *5. Prepare the Dressing & Extras* * Dressing: Mix 1/2 cup Greek yogurt with 4 grated garlic cloves, black pepper, salt, and chopped coriander. * Tomato Salad: Toss halved cherry tomatoes with a little salt and lemon juice. * Avocado: Slice one fresh avocado or mash it with onions and lime to make guacamole. Assembling the Burrito Bowl * Rice Base: Press the Cilantro Lime Rice into a small bowl and flip it onto the center of your serving plate/bowl. * Arrange Sides: Place the sautéed paneer, rajma, sautéed salad, cherry tomato salad, and avocado slices in sections around the rice. * Final Touch: Add a generous dollop of the garlic yogurt dressing. * Garnish: Serve with a side of tortilla chips or nachos for crunch and a lemon wedge. *Enjoy* your homemade, healthy, and vibrant Veg Burrito Bowl! 👍
